spec.user_stories: - As the sole user, I create a log with a description and 1-5 photos so I can record my day. - As the user, I view all previous logs, newest first, each showing date, description and photos. - As the user, I edit a log's description and add/remove photos while keeping 1-5 photos. - As the user, I delete a log and have its image files removed from disk too. - As the user, I want my logs to survive application restarts. - As the user, I want invalid uploads and over-limit requests rejected with clear errors.
spec.acceptance_criteria: 1. Creating a log with a non-blank description and 1-5 valid photos succeeds; the response includes id, description, photo URLs/paths, created_at and updated_at. Pass: success status and fields present. 2. Creating with a missing or blank (whitespace-only) description is rejected with a 4xx validation error and nothing is stored. 3. Creating with 0 photos or more than 5 photos is rejected with a 4xx error; nothing is stored and no files remain in uploads/. 4. Only JPG, JPEG, PNG, WEBP files are accepted (extension and content type/real content checked). Any other file (e.g. .gif, .txt, or a non-image renamed to .jpg) is rejected with 4xx and nothing is stored. 5. A photo larger than 5 MB (5 * 1024 * 1024 bytes) is rejected with 4xx; exactly 5 MB is accepted. The oversize request is also rejected and nothing is persisted. 6. Each stored photo gets a unique generated filename in uploads/; uploading two files with the same original name never overwrites either. 7. created_at is set automatically on create. updated_at equals created_at at creation and is changed to the current time on each successful edit; created_at never changes on edit. 8. Listing logs returns all logs ordered newest first by created_at, each with date, description and photos; an empty store returns an empty list. 9. Fetching a single log by id returns it; a nonexistent id returns 404. 10. Editing a log can change the description, remove existing photos and add new ones in one request. The final photo count must be 1-5; otherwise 4xx and the log and its files are unchanged. A blank description is rejected on edit. Edits to a nonexistent id return 404. 11. Photos removed during an edit are deleted from disk; if the edit fails validation, no files are added or deleted. 12. Deleting a log removes the DB row and all its image files from uploads/; subsequent GET returns 404. Deleting a nonexistent id returns 404. 13. Data (descriptions, timestamps, photo paths) is stored in SQLite and photos in uploads/; after restarting the app all logs and photos are still available and viewable. 14. Uploaded photos are served over HTTP so the frontend can display them. 15. The frontend (HTML/CSS/JS) served by the app lets the user create, view (newest-first simple list showing date, description, photos), edit and delete logs through the HTTP API, and displays server validation errors to the user. Delete asks for confirmation. 16. No login/logout and no search or date filter exist. 17. pytest tests cover the API endpoints and validation rules above (create, list, get, edit, delete, photo count/format/size limits, 404s, file cleanup, timestamps) and run against an isolated temporary database and uploads directory, not the real data.
spec.assumptions: - Single-user, no authentication; app runs locally. - Project code lives in C:/Users/Ivan/Desktop/A-Finals (outside .claude/), uploads/ at project root. - "Date" shown is created_at formatted for display (updated_at shown additionally when edited is optional). - Ordering is by created_at descending, ties broken by id descending. - Description has no stated max length; a reasonable generous cap (e.g. several thousand characters) may be applied by the implementer but is not required. - Total request size limit follows from 5 photos x 5 MB plus overhead; oversize requests are rejected with 413 or 422. - Photos remain in the order uploaded. - Photo validation checks real file content, not only the extension. - No pagination in v1.
spec.edge_cases: - Exactly 1 and exactly 5 photos accepted; 0 and 6 rejected. - Edit that removes all existing photos without adding new ones is rejected; edit removing 4 of 5 and adding 4 new is accepted. - Edit that would exceed 5 (existing kept + new) is rejected. - Uppercase extensions (.JPG, .PNG) accepted. - Filenames with path traversal characters or odd Unicode in the original name cannot escape uploads/. - One invalid file among several valid ones rejects the entire request with no partial storage. - A DB row whose file is already missing on disk does not make delete or edit fail. - Failure partway through create/edit leaves no orphaned files. - Removing a photo id that does not belong to the log is rejected or ignored with a defined 4xx behavior. - Concurrent restart: uploads/ and the DB are created automatically if missing.

risks.risk: Keeping DB and filesystem consistent on failures during edit/delete (orphan files or dangling rows).
Enforcing the 5 MB limit without fully buffering oversized uploads in memory.
Content-type/extension spoofing; mitigated by content verification.
Timezone ambiguity in timestamps; assume UTC stored, displayed in local time.

spec.dependencies: Python, FastAPI, an ASGI server (e.g. uvicorn), python-multipart for uploads, SQLite (stdlib), pytest and an HTTP test client (httpx), optionally Pillow for content verification; uploads/ directory.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: create (1-6), view (8,9,15), edit (10,11), delete (12), persistence (13), rejection (2-5). Each criterion is observable via API or tests. Biggest uncertainty: the exact edit request shape and error codes are left to the implementer, and the timestamp display timezone is assumed; neither is blocking.
